newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares fall on petrol price hikes.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares fall on petrol price hikes.

text.p: Istanbul shares extended losses on Monday over worries that interest rates and inflation could rise after an increase in petroleum prices, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,952, down 52 points, or 2.59 percent from Friday's close after trading in a broad band of 2,023 and 1,943.
Daily volume fell 14 percent to 16.84 trillion lira ($103 million), from Friday's 19.58 trillion ($120 million).
Ismail Guner from Info Securities said the bearish sentiment was mainly due to petroleum product price rises and the absence of fresh expectations after completion of first half company results.
"There are worries for higher inflation data after petroleum price hikes on Sunday. This will negatively affect August monthly inflation and will raise interest rates" Guner said.
The government raised petroleum product prices by seven to nine percent on Sunday.

Of the 251 shares traded, 170 declined, 41 advanced and 40 ended stable. The IMKB Industrial dropped 1.65 percent to 1,902, the IMKB Services lost 3.12 percent to 1,928 and the IMKB Financial lost 3.27 percent to 2,097.

The top actives of the day were largely state-owned flat steel producer Eregli, down 500 lira at 27,000 lira, Turkish Telecom. Alcatel, up 500 lira to 32,000 and textile producer Koytas up 750 lira at 12,000.
They made up 19 percent of the total volume.
